headline: South Asia: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
- India: Saudi-Led Coalition Intercepts Drones, Missiles Targeted At Riyadh.
- Western Russia: One killed, six injured and buildings damaged in Russian attacks on Ukraine's west and centre – video.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
- Military Times, 2 hours ago: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
The Army's 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated as the service reshapes its PSYOP and information warfare forces to counter global adversaries.
- Military Times, 10 hours ago: What is the US Army doing in Panama? A bit of everything..
As Washington shifts its attention toward the Western Hemisphere, a reinvigorated jungle school is just one part of the evolving U.S. presence in Panama.
- Military Times, 6 hours ago: ‘Weaponized light’: KBR’s new base defense technology pits lasers against drones.
The Pentagon recently selected KBR's Firefly system for a pilot program to test defending U.S. military installations against adversarial drones.
The Caribbean - bottom line: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 15 hours ago: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
A 19-year-old man has been charged with three counts of murder in connection with last Friday’s deadly attack on Kidd Lane, off Spanish Town Road in St Andrew, which claimed the lives of two women and a one-year-old boy. The accused, Dante Davis, who has addresses on Spanish Town Road and Kidd Lane in Kingston 13, is also facing charges of conspiracy to commit murder, arson, conspiracy to commit arson, possession of a prohibited weapon, unauthorised possession of ammunition and using a firearm to commit a felony.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: One killed, six injured and buildings damaged in Russian attacks on Ukraine's west and centre – video.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: One killed, six injured and buildings damaged in Russian attacks on Ukraine's west and centre – video.
Regional authorities have reported strikes on Rivne, Kovel, Vinnytsia and Prykarpattia, resulting in power cuts, infrastructure fires and five injuries.
- The Moscow Times, Ukrainska Pravda, South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 3 hours ago: Russia Repels 644 Ukrainian Drones as Trump Calls Attacks on Russian Refineries ‘Disgrace’.
Russian strikes also left 370,000 residents in Ukraine’s northwestern Volyn region without electricity.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Russian General Staff announces start of massive strikes on Ukraine's energy grid.
Valery Gerasimov has stated that Russian forces have begun large-scale attacks on Ukrainian energy facilities amid ongoing power supply disruptions.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Zelenskyy and Finnish PM discuss Russian strikes and Ukraine's need for shelters.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo have discussed enhancing civil protection, building shelters and countering Russian attacks.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Democracy Digest: Polish Man Charged With Plotting to Kill PM, Suspected Saboteurs Arrested.
- Balkan Insight, 14 hours ago: Democracy Digest: Polish Man Charged With Plotting to Kill PM, Suspected Saboteurs Arrested.
Elsewhere, Slovakia to revive cooperation with Russia at meeting planned for November 25; Hungary parliament approves new child protection legislation; and Czech Army chief warns of possible Russian attack
- Politico Europe, 7 hours ago: Zelenskyy warns 20M Ukrainians could flee to Europe if Russia wins war.
The stark warning comes as Kyiv heads into a brutal winter and faces a cash crunch.
- Politico Europe, 7 hours ago: Denmark, Italy, Poland urge EU leaders to harden stance on irregular migration.
Draft conclusions backed by Rome, Warsaw and Copenhagen say irregular migration is "negatively linked to crime rates."
- Politico Europe, 9 hours ago: France, Germany strike bargain on Made in Europe, car emissions.
The compromise was reached after the German Social Democrats, the junior coalition partner in Friedrich Merz’s government, dropped their opposition.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: Drone Attack Kills Two in North Darfur As Red Crescent Volunteer Killed in Blue Nile.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 15 hours ago: Sudan: Drone Attack Kills Two in North Darfur As Red Crescent Volunteer Killed in Blue Nile.
[Dabanga] Furawiya / Karnoi / El Tina / Umm Darfa / El Rosei -- Drone attack in Furawiya area of North Darfur kills two and injures eight, while a Red Crescent volunteer dies in a bombing in Blue Nile and South Darfur authorities impose sweeping emergency measures.
- Africanews, 8 hours ago: Russian missiles spark huge factory fires in Ukraine’s Odesa and Zaporizhzhia.
Russian strikes ignited massive fires at businesses in Odesa and Zaporizhzhia as President Zelensky met European leaders for talks.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 10 hours ago: Nigeria: Soldiers, Terrorists Killed in Midnight Terror Attack On Borno Military Base.
[Premium Times] Sources said 15 soldiers and five members of the Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF) were killed in the encounter.
- Africanews, 5 hours ago: Ethiopian gains in Tigray risk wider war with Eritrea, analyst warns.
Ethiopia’s military advances in northern Tigray do not spell an end to the conflict but have the potential to increase the risk of war with neighboring Eritrea, an analyst with knowledge of the region has warned
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: 'We'll knock it out fast': Trump threatens Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site with strikes.
- Jerusalem Post, Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: 'We'll knock it out fast': Trump threatens Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site with strikes.
Trump did not confirm previous reports that the US would use a GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb (MOAB), colloquially known as the "mother of all bombs," to strike Iran.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Ukraine president targets Trump, Putin at EU summit.
President Zelenskyy warned Russia’s ambitions extend beyond eastern Ukraine, saying its drone attack threaten NATO.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 6 hours ago: How Israeli firm’s ‘zero-click’ malware attack poses global security risk.
A new ‘zero-click’ hack uses ads to target victims without any action needed on their part.
- Jerusalem Post, 3 hours ago: IDF kills Hamas Nukhba commander in Gaza who infiltrated Re'im base on October 7.
Since the October 7 attacks, the terrorist continued his involvement in planning terror attacks against Israeli soldiers and civilians, the military noted.
South Africa - bottom line: South Africa: Katherine O'regan Receives George Bizos Human Rights Award, Warns of Shift to Authoritarianism.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 9 hours ago: South Africa: Katherine O'regan Receives George Bizos Human Rights Award, Warns of Shift to Authoritarianism.
[Daily Maverick] On 15 October, former Constitutional Court Justice Katherine O'Regan received the George Bizos Human Rights Award, reflecting on the project of democracy and urging resistance to rising authoritarianism.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 13 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Poverty, Injustice Threaten Lasting Peace in Zimbabwe - ZPP.
[263Chat] The Zimbabwe Peace Project (ZPP) has called for greater investment in justice, human rights and inclusive institutions warning that poverty, inequality and weak access to justice continue to threaten lasting peace in Zimbabwe.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its “sovereignty, security and territorial integrity” amid a recent escalation in Houthi attacks. According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the premier made the remarks during a meeting with newly appointed Saudi Ambassador Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy. He welcomed the envoy to Pakistan and congratulated him on assuming his new responsibilities.
- The Hindu - International, 10 hours ago: Airstrikes, artillery hit north Ethiopia as government and rebels clash, sources say.
Air attacks killed at least 17 people northwest of Tigray’s capital Mekelle — which federal government forces took over the weekend — according to a bulletin circulated among humanitarian groups
- The Hindu - International, 13 hours ago: Drone strikes in the Black Sea raise fears of Russian escalation to test NATO's response.
The attacks in the two countries' exclusive economic zones threaten a global shipping route and have left two people dead, with at least 25 still missing. They also run the risk of drawing other countries directly into the war for Ukraine
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Kohat Police Lines attack mastermind killed in joint operation in KP's Lakki Marwat: CTD.
LAKKI MARWAT: The Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) said on Friday that its personnel had killed a terrorist commander in a joint operation with security forces in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Lakki Marwat on Friday. The CTD said in a statement that the slain terrorist, whom the law enforcement department identified as Zahid Gul, was the mastermind of the attack on Kohat Police Lines. In the attack on Sept 18, an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, following which terrorists stormed the compound and attacked police facilities.
India - bottom line: Saudi-Led Coalition Intercepts Drones, Missiles Targeted At Riyadh.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Saudi-Led Coalition Intercepts Drones, Missiles Targeted At Riyadh.
Since Yemen's civil war flared back to life in July, the Houthis have repeatedly struck Saudi targets including Red Sea tankers, oil facilities and Riyadh's international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Zelenskyy slams Trump's diesel deal, says will help fund Putin’s war in Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concerns over the US diesel deal with Russia. He warned that this agreement could provide additional funds for Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine. Zelenskyy emphasized the need for Europe to increase support to Ukraine as missile attacks continue. The president requested significant financial assistance to maintain Ukraine's defense against Russian aggression.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Two vessels carrying 24 Indian seafarers hit by projectiles, drone in separate incidents.
Union shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed that two vessels carrying Indian seafarers were attacked in October. The MT ST 3 was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, while the YARA J was hit by a drone off Romania. Fortunately, all 24 Indian nationals aboard both vessels are reported safe and unharmed. India has condemned attacks on commercial vessels, citing concerns for the safety of seafarers.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: US temple plot, school shooting: Gun epidemic spares no one as debate goes off target.
A neo-Nazi teen attempted a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois, but his rifle jammed. The attack highlights ongoing debates about gun violence and societal issues, including parenting and mental health. Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi expressed horror that the attack targeted Indian Americans during worship. Many lawmakers condemned the incident, emphasizing the need to address religious and racial hatred in society.
Asia - bottom line: EU rallies around Zelensky as rift widens with Trump over Russia energy strikes.
- South China Morning Post - China, 10 hours ago: EU rallies around Zelensky as rift widens with Trump over Russia energy strikes.
European leaders on Friday rallied around Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky as Kyiv’s ties with US President Donald Trump have nosedived and worries grow that US leader is increasingly siding with Russia. Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since last week, when Trump eased sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel onto global markets. Zelensky infuriated Trump further by ordering Ukraine’s forces to restart strikes on Russian oil refineries in...
- South China Morning Post - China, 16 hours ago: More than music: Hong Kong Chinese Orchestra strikes a chord across generations.
For nearly five decades, the Hong Kong Chinese Orchestra has worked to bring its music to a wider audience, including people who might never have considered entering a concert hall. Executive director Celina Chin Man-wah said the orchestra had long sought to ensure Chinese music was not seen as distant, formal or difficult to understand. That has meant commissioning new works, exploring different musical styles and developing programmes for younger audiences. “We cannot rely on the old...
- South China Morning Post - China, 16 hours ago: Chilling details emerge of mass shooting plot targeting US Hindu temple.
Illinois authorities believe a 19-year-old man charged with planning a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in suburban Chicago entered the building’s car park on Sunday, hours before police arrested him near his home after receiving a tip about the alleged attack plan. Authorities announced Wednesday that they had arrested Alexandros Paporakis and provided the additional detail about his suspected movement during a news conference Thursday. The leaders of Sri Venkateswara Swami (Balaji) Temple in a...
- South China Morning Post - China, 10 hours ago: China leans in to hi-tech systems to counter emerging AI-fuelled terror threats.
China revealed AI-powered drone interceptors and other uncrewed systems at an international counterterrorism forum in Beijing this week, as security experts warned that new technologies could enable new forms of terrorism. The equipment was on display at the Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counterterrorism, which ran from Tuesday to Thursday and was attended by more than 320 defence experts and military delegates from 62 countries. North Korea’s top missile commander accused South Korea of making false claims about a recent hypersonic missile test, according to a short interview released Thursday, drawing a prompt rebuttal from Seoul. DPRK Missile Administration General Director Jang Chang Ha said “It is hard to believe that [South Korea’s hypersonic glide vehicle (HGV)] underwent hypersonic flight” […]

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: At least three killed by Russian drones in Ukraine which cut power to 370,000.
- ABC News Australia, 7 hours ago: At least three killed by Russian drones in Ukraine which cut power to 370,000.
At least three people were killed by Russian drones in Ukraine overnight, the strikes also hit two shopping centres and key energy grid infrastructure.
- The Guardian - Australia, 6 hours ago: EVs are holding value better than expected – and it has a lot to do with Australia’s cost of living.
The appeal of electric vehicles is financial as much as environmental for many drivers Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here The electric vehicles were splattered after a concrete spray incident, but repairable. Eager to recoup their costs, insurers sent the 40 BYD vehicles to an auction run by asset sales company Pickles in late March. With fuel prices soaring in response to the US and Israel war on Iran, a bidding frenzy erupted. Continue reading...
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Inside Russell Brand's trial, where he was called a 'maniac' and 'predator'.
The world-famous actor and comedian appeared calm and almost zen-like as he sat in the dock at Southwark Crown Court, and the prosecution began unfolding its case against him.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of Normal People, Bridgerton and a famous disease.
Each question in the ABC 50/50 quiz has only two options: one is right, the other is wrong. But be warned: somewhere there lurks a trap.
